reflection: Volume-based relative/market factors (AAPL vs NVDA volume, QQQ volume surge, NVDA range) are the only ones that joined; they help in 2023 and 2025 and often hurt in 2024. One-day intraday/close-location and gap factors flip sign across years and fail. I will try more volume-regime and range-relative features, smoothed to reduce noise, and partner them with the team's volume/range factors using different roles (apple_own, relative_move). I'll avoid directional one-day intraday quantities.

lessons.name: log_aapl_nvda_volume_ratio_z20
lessons.lesson: Standardizing the log AAPL/NVDA volume ratio removed the volume-spike skew and gave steady gains for both models in 3 of 4 years, so relative volume is real signal.

lessons.name: aapl_close_loc_3d_mean
lessons.lesson: A 3-day close location is too noisy and overlaps with 3-day mean return, so it only helped in 2023.

lessons.name: aapl_intraday_minus_overnight_5d
lessons.lesson: Intraday-versus-overnight return split helped LR in 2022-23 but reversed in 2024-25, so the pattern is not stable across regimes.

lessons.name: nvda_range_vs_aapl_range
lessons.lesson: NVDA's range relative to Apple's captures sector-vs-Apple turbulence and helped both models in 3 years, but only added value in combination with QQQ volume surge.

lessons.name: qqq_range_expansion_vs_aapl_volume
lessons.lesson: QQQ range expansion ratio is near-noise for direction alone and only gave extra value in a pair, not enough to stand.

lessons.name: aapl_msft_volume_gap_signed_close_loc
lessons.lesson: The MSFT-minus-NVDA close location difference is a noisy one-day intraday quantity with little relation to Apple's next move.

factors.name: qqq_volume_surge_5d_smooth
factors.hypothesis: The one-day QQQ volume surge was noisy and hurt in 2022 and 2024; a 5d-vs-60d volume ratio captures persistent stress regimes and should be more stable.

factors.name: log_aapl_nvda_volume_ratio_z60
factors.hypothesis: The 20d z-score failed in 2024, probably because the baseline adapts too fast; a 60d baseline gives a steadier relative-volume deviation.

factors.name: aapl_range_zscore_20
factors.hypothesis: Apple's range relative to its own recent norm flags unusual intraday turbulence, which often precedes mean reversion; it is normalised unlike the raw daily range.

factors.name: qqq_msft_volume_ratio_z20
factors.hypothesis: Abnormal QQQ volume versus MSFT volume shows when flows are index-driven rather than stock-specific, which changes how Apple follows the market.

factors.name: aapl_volume_trend_5_60
factors.hypothesis: A slow Apple volume regime measure complements the range-based market-turbulence factor by showing whether Apple itself is seeing heightened participation.

factors.name: aapl_minus_qqq_5d_vs_volume_z
factors.hypothesis: Apple's 5d relative move matters more when volume is unusual; interacting it with a volume z-score gives the team's volume factor a directional partner.
